newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest set for more favorable harvest weather.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest set for more favorable harvest weather.

text.p: Weather in the U.S. Midwest looks set to remain favorable for harvesting of corn and soybeans over the next few days after the weekend's warm, sunny conditions, meteorologists said.
"There are no signs of any harvest-disrupting rains in sight," said Mike Palmerino, senior agricultural meteorologist for Weather Services Corp.
Palmerino noted that there was light rainfall early Monday as a cold front moved into the U.S. Midwest but the amount of harvest disruption was likely to be "minimal".
The heaviest concentration was in southeast Iowa, where rainfall was up to 0.5 inch. Rain in northern Missouri, western Iowa and eastern Nebraska was mostly less than 0.1 inch, Palmerino said.
Showers will move into the eastern corn belt late Monday but rain will be 0.25 inch or less, he added.

The cold front will bring freezing temperatures to southeast Minnesota, northern Iowa and western Wisconsin early Tuesday, but be restricted to areas already hit by frost and so will do little further damage, Palmerino said.
Weather will be cool and dry from Tuesday until conditions warm up toward the end of the week with a few more light showers on Friday night throughout the corn belt, he added.
"It looks pretty ideal for harvest. We've got below normal precipitation for the next 10 days," said Fred Gesser, chief forecaster for Weather Express.
Both Gesser and Palmerino said tropical storm Josephine, which is likely to be upgraded to a hurricane later Monday, was unlikely to bring much rain to the U.S. Midwest.
"I think it (the impact) is going to be pretty much restricted to the (U.S.) East Coast," Gesser said.
Gesser said temperatures would overall be about normal, with cold weather early in the week but warmer conditions toward the end of the week.
He said he expected the next system to bring a trace to 0.5 inch of rain to the western corn belt on Saturday and Sunday and the eastern belt Sunday and Monday with about 20 percent coverage.
